new_title: Arsenal v Leeds LIVE: Result and reaction after champions fight to Premier League win

The Premier League returns with champions Arsenal hosting high-flying Leeds in the first fixture after the seismic Manchester City verdict.
Arsenal are second in the table with four wins from their opening five matches but were heavily, and easily, beaten by Brighton last time out as they went down 3-0 at the Amex Stadium. Fresh from signing a new contract that will keep him at the Emirates until 2030, Arteta must now sweep that defeat aside as he looks to keep pace with current league leaders Manchester City - though there is plenty of uncertainty about how the rest of this season may pan out after recent news.
Leeds, meanwhile, remain unbeaten this season, winning twice and drawing their other three fixtures so far. They will expect to have to be at their best after making the trip south to London, though, as they go in search of a statement success.
Follow all of the latest from the Premier League clash with our live blog below:
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 45 + 1 minutes
Into three additional minutes at the end of a first half probably edged by Leeds.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 44 minutes
Another sharp stop! David Raya is again required to make himself big to prevent Gabriel Gudmundsson thumping home on the bounce after another cross caused a spot of chaos along the line of the six-yard box.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 43 minutes
Two good bits of defending from Leeds' booked duo: Ao Tanaka and Ethan Ampadu both would have been in bother had they not got the ball with challenges on the retreat.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 42 minutes
That lifts the home fans a touch, Noni Madueke's curving cross flicked over the bar by Kai Havertz. Mikel Arteta scribbles a few thoughts on his notepaper.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 41 minutes
Arsenal just need to find their flow again. Leeds have totally drained the energy of the Emirates, which is very, very quiet at the moment.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 38 minutes
That's two central midfielders booked, though, which is an area of concern for the visitors. Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu is shown a yellow card for a similar foul to that which resulted in Ao Tanaka receiving the same sanction.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 36 minutes
Raya is pressed into service again and rounded by Noah Okafor - though the Leeds forward is offside. Daniel Farke will be very, very pleased wth the manner in which his team are threatening the champions, though - and perhaps disappointed they've not made more of these chances.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 36 minutes
Ao Tanaka receives the game's first booking, felling Myles Lewis-Skelly in transition...but only after Leeds pass up another great chance, Anton Stach all alone in space but not found with David Raya rushing out well to smother the danger.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 34 minutes
Almost! Anton Stach delivers a long diagonal free kick into the Arsenal box, which David Raya comes all of 16 yards to punch. His contact is poor, though, and the Spaniard has to be very, very hasty in retreating to ensure a header back the other way does not beat him back to the line. Ethan Ampadu was the would-be scorer; Raya was there in the nick of time to deny him.
Raya soon shows the other side of his game, though, with a fabulous pass to spark an Arsenal attack that doesn't quite fully materialise.
Arsenal 0-0 Leeds, 33 minutes
A patched-up Justin is ready to return but unable to do so as Arsenal win back possession high up the pitch. Referee Paul Tierney eventually grants him the chance to rejoin the Leeds defensive effort as Ao Tanaka does his job towards the opposite sideline, winning a one-on-one duel and then drawing a foul.

Arsenal fought back from behind to secure a hard-earned win over Leeds United on their Premier League return.
After an extended international break, Mikel Arteta's side struggled to find fluency against the impressive visitors, and looked like they might slip to a second successive defeat when James Justin fired Leeds into a deserved second-half lead. But Riccardo Calafiori soon levelled affairs, before Bruno Guimaraes finished off a stunning team goal to take the three points.
Guimaraes had been used off the bench in an illustration of the squad depth available to Arteta, overseeing his first game since signing a new contract at the club. Victory leaves the champions level on points with Manchester City, who play on Sunday, at the top of the table - although it remains to be seen what punishment their title rivals could face after the seismic verdict.
Follow all of the latest from the Premier League clash with our live blog below:
The Bruno Guimaraes moment that showed why Arsenal remain Premier League favourites
Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.
After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.
However, Riccardo Calafiori drew the champions level when he converted Ben White's header from close range in the 62nd minute, before substitute Bruno Guimaraes struck the decisive blow just six minutes after he came off the bench.
Mikel Arteta offers his thoughts
"Before the game, we talked about two things: the challenge ahead, and to restore our identity and be ourselves again," the Arsenal boss says. "We weren't pleased with what we did against Brighton, and today was a chance to put that right. We reacted in the manner we expected.
"They are extremely well organised, very physical, committed in everything they do. They are a threat. You keep fouling them or give them throw-ins and set-pieces, they are incredible with the way they attack the box. They could have punished us in the first half. This is a testament to the league.
"When you play 12.30 at home and go 1-0 down, you have to restore a lot of things. The energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. It made a difference to help us win the game."
And here is Bruno Guimaraes speaking to TNT Sports
"I feel unbelievable. Against Brighton, we were not at the right level and today the mentality was mostly back. An important goal, three important points, I'm very happy.
"It's a great feeling. It's important that when I am on the pitch I give my best and a bit of a headache for the manager. Three points is always welcome.
"It's a new challenge for me. For me, the most important thing for Bruno is to go on the pitch and play my football."
FT: Arsenal 2-1 Leeds
A hard-fought success for Arsenal, but three points nonetheless. Below their best for an hour, Mikel Arteta's side lifted their level to come from behind after James Justin's opener - and it obviously helps to have players of Bruno Guimaraes' quality to come on.
Here is that lovely winner:
Arsenal 2-1 Leeds, 90 + 5 minutes
It should have been three! Bukayo Saka is sprung by Viktor Gyokeres, but can't beat James Trafford in the one-on-one situation. He seemed a touch hesitant, oddly, and Trafford palms it away.
Still, that'll be that!
Arsenal 2-1 Leeds, 90 + 4 minutes
Leeds throw bodies forward and the ball follows them via Ethan Ampadu's long hurl from the touchline. Arsenal have it well marshalled.
Arsenal 2-1 Leeds, 90 + 2 minutes
Why has Viktor Gyokeres not hit it? James Trafford gets himself in a right mess 35 yards from goal, leaving it agape as Gyokeres dispossesses him. The striker appears to open up the angle for a shot, but chooses not to, twisting and turning unnecessarily before eventually running aground.
Curious. That's the sort of opportunity forwards usually gobble up.
Arsenal 2-1 Leeds, 90 minutes
The last Arsenal change is another sign of their depth: World Cup winner Mikel Merino replaces Martin Odegaard.
Five more minutes between them and victory.
